forces.title: Evolving customer journey with provisional bookings and post-booking reshopping
forces.description: Travelers increasingly view booking confirmations as provisional, not final, with 40% changing accommodations post-booking. This behavior is driven by flexible policies, continuous price monitoring, and a constant stream of new recommendations. This structural shift means hotel operators must maintain engagement post-booking, as 78% of travelers continue planning and researching after initial reservations, creating both a retention challenge and an opportunity for incremental spend via social media.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI becoming a primary channel for initial travel inspiration
forces.description: AI tools and search engines are rapidly emerging as significant sources of initial travel inspiration, utilized in 25% of inspiration sessions. This creates new 'front doors' for travelers, expanding the number of touchpoints where destination and hotel ideas can arise. While this offers more opportunities for hotels to enter a traveler's consideration set, it also intensifies competition and requires adaptive content strategies to be visible in these new channels.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Travelers reluctant to delegate hotel bookings to AI without human trust
forces.description: While 62% of travelers find AI helpful for planning, discomfort significantly increases when AI moves from advising to acting. Only half are comfortable with AI making a hotel booking, and 75% prefer to finalize bookings themselves. Factors increasing confidence include the ability to review/change details, accurate recommendation track records, human intervention for disruptions, and personalized understanding. This indicates a strong preference for human assurance at high-stakes transaction points, limiting full AI adoption in direct booking.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Social media and content creators drive destination interest and incremental spend
forces.description: Social media content influences 7 out of 10 travelers to consider new destinations, disconnected from initial travel intent. Post-booking, social content leads to 60% of travelers adding activities, 41% extending trips, and 22% choosing more expensive options. Travel creators and influencers are among the top three trusted sources for 67% of travelers, demonstrating significant power to inspire and drive incremental spend throughout the customer journey for hotels and destinations.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Authentic customer content and transparency boost conversion
forces.description: Research indicates that surfacing genuine customer feedback, real guest experiences, and user-generated content (even with imperfections) significantly increases traveler confidence and drives conversion for hotels. This transparency about real-life situations and relatable experiences is more effective than purely curated brand narratives, demonstrating a shift in consumer trust towards peer-generated proof over brand-produced marketing materials.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI-driven visibility challenge for hotel offerings in fragmented search results
forces.description: Hotel operators face a critical challenge as AI becomes a 'new front door' to travel planning. AI tools often surface only a narrow selection of properties, potentially excluding strong offerings if content is poorly distributed or not optimized for machine interpretation (Generative Engine Optimization - GEO). The fragmentation of AI answers, where different tools yield different 'best' picks, also erodes traveler confidence and increases the burden of reconciliation, posing a significant risk for hotel discoverability.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Shortened booking lead times create revenue management challenges
forces.description: Hotel operators in Ireland are observing a trend of shortened booking windows and an increase in last-minute bookings. This shift in consumer behavior presents significant challenges for traditional revenue management strategies, requiring greater agility and sophisticated tools to optimize pricing and inventory. Operators need to adapt their forecasting and pricing models to effectively manage this compressed booking cycle and its impact on revenue predictability.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Stronger competition for hotels from Airbnb platforms
forces.description: Norwegian hotels are experiencing increased competitive pressure from alternative accommodation platforms like Airbnb. This growth in peer-to-peer lodging options diversifies the market and offers travelers more choices, potentially impacting traditional hotels' occupancy rates and pricing power. Operators must differentiate their offerings and adapt strategies to retain market share amidst this evolving landscape.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Rising labor costs and availability issues constrain margins
forces.description: The Irish hospitality sector faces significant pressure from increasing wage costs, with average wages reaching 39.5% of turnover in 2024 (up from 38.5% in 2023), coupled with persistent labor availability challenges. These factors directly constrain margin recovery and force operators to critically review staffing requirements and adopt more efficient labor scheduling to mitigate the impact on profitability.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical uncertainty risks international visitor sentiment and airfares
forces.description: The ongoing Middle East conflict presents potential risks to Ireland's hospitality sector, primarily by influencing international visitor sentiment and potentially driving higher airfares. While Ireland benefits from a diversified demand base (EU, North America, UK) and strong domestic tourism, a sustained deterioration in geopolitical conditions could weigh on inbound and corporate travel confidence, particularly for high-value long-haul demand.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Value-conscious consumers demand differentiated experiences and visible value
forces.description: Consumer behavior is recalibrating, with guests increasingly scrutinizing value. While they remain willing to spend on clear, differentiated, and dependable experiences, high value scrutiny places pressure on hotel operators. This necessitates balancing rate growth with consistent service, product quality, and visibly communicated value propositions to protect pricing power and maintain relevance in a competitive market.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Gradual return of State-contracted accommodation boosts capacity
forces.description: The phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation (due by March 2027), which saw bed stock fall from 13.0% in Summer 2023 to 3.7% in May 2026, is gradually returning to tourism supply. This provides a measured supply-side tailwind, improving overall destination capacity for commercial tourism and supporting market availability in affected regions across Ireland.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Improved air access supports inbound tourism recovery
forces.description: Ireland has seen significant improvements in air seat capacity, with a 15% increase in winter and a projected 3% rise above Summer 2025 levels (including +5% from GB and +9% from US). This enhanced air access directly supports the inbound tourism recovery, contributing to an 18% year-on-year increase in trips to Ireland for the five months to May 2026, boosting demand for hotels.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Increasing adoption of technology for operational efficiency and margins
forces.description: Technology adoption is becoming essential for Irish hospitality operators, moving from optional to operational. Investments in AI, automation, advanced revenue management tools, and energy monitoring are critical for protecting service standards and improving margins. This structural shift highlights a focus on using technology to reduce operational friction, optimize processes like rostering and guest communications, and manage costs more effectively.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Market polarization towards luxury/lifestyle and budget/value segments
forces.description: The Irish hospitality market is experiencing increased polarization, with the strongest investor and customer momentum concentrated at the luxury/lifestyle and budget/value ends. This trend puts pressure on mid-market and larger independent hotels to develop clearer positioning, seek brand affiliation, or offer experience-led differentiation to maintain relevance and pricing power, reflecting a fundamental shift in consumer preferences and investment focus.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Reduced inflow of Asian tourists due to travel disruptions
forces.description: Norwegian tourism contacts are reporting a reduced inflow of tourists from Asia, along with cancellations and deferrals from this demographic. This downturn is attributed to factors such as cancelled flights and geopolitical hostilities (specifically, the outbreak of hostilities in Iran). This presents a headwind for hotels and other tourism-related businesses relying on international visitors, particularly from long-haul markets.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Stronger krone dampens tourism growth prospects
forces.description: Many contacts in the Norwegian household services sector, including tourism, anticipate that the stronger krone exchange rate will dampen growth. A stronger local currency makes Norway a more expensive destination for international tourists, potentially reducing their purchasing power and discouraging travel. This acts as a headwind against the sector's overall growth, despite positive underlying activity.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 2/2026: Recruitment difficulties have eased somewhat

viewpoints.title: AI adoption for travel planning outpaces hotel operator readiness for booking
viewpoints.description: McKinsey observes that AI is rapidly advancing in travel planning and discovery, yet hotel operators are not adapting quickly enough. While AI aids inspiration and comparison, travelers are reluctant to trust it for actual bookings or disruption handling, preferring human interaction. This creates a new visibility challenge for operators if their offerings don't surface in AI answers, but also presents opportunities for those who structure content for Generative Engine Optimization.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Trust-building through genuine customer reviews drives hotel conversion rates
viewpoints.description: Alix Boulnois, Chief Commercial, Digital, and Tech Officer at Accor, states that transparent and authentic customer feedback, including user-generated content and reviews (even negative ones), significantly drives conversion rates for hotels. This approach creates more confidence among customers than presenting a purely curated brand narrative, highlighting the importance of relatable, real-life guest experiences over polished marketing.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Irish hospitality H2 2026 outlook cautiously positive, focused on margin conversion
viewpoints.description: The H2 2026 outlook for the Irish hospitality sector is cautiously positive, with an emphasis on converting RevPAR growth into cashflow. Operators face challenges from shifting supply, value-conscious consumers, and persistent cost inflation, requiring disciplined cost control, strategic channel mix, and efficient payroll/energy management to maintain profitability rather than solely pursuing volume recovery. Trading momentum is positive, but sustained success depends on operational discipline.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish accommodation shows strong performance, rate-led growth
viewpoints.description: The accommodation segment in Ireland is performing strongly in 2026 YTD, with both value and volume growing, supported by resilient hotel demand and rate discipline. This positive trend contrasts with the food services sector, which faces a more challenging environment due to a shift towards value-conscious consumers and limited-service restaurants. This indicates a bifurcation in the hospitality market, with hotels generally faring better.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Gradual return of state-contracted beds will not immediately dilute pricing power
viewpoints.description: Fáilte Ireland reports a significant reduction in State-contracted accommodation, with registered tourism bed stock under such contracts falling from 13.0% in summer 2023 to 3.7% in May 2026. While this phased withdrawal by March 2027 should gradually improve tourism accommodation availability, it is not expected to cause a uniform or immediate uplift in commercial supply or materially dilute current hotel pricing power.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish hospitality faces high insolvency risk due to tightening profitability
viewpoints.description: The Irish hospitality sector, encompassing pubs and restaurants, is projected to experience a continued high proportion of insolvencies through the remainder of 2026. This pessimistic outlook is attributed to profitability tightening, driven by persistently rising fuel prices and increased processing and transport costs, exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. Smaller operators are particularly advised to focus on careful cash-flow forecasting.

viewpoints.title: Norwegian tourism reports solid activity and high guest counts
viewpoints.description: Household-oriented service contacts in Norway, including hotels, restaurants, and amusement parks, are reporting solid activity and high guest counts. This positive performance was partly boosted by events linked to the football World Cup at the beginning of summer, indicating robust demand within the tourism sector despite some concerns about reduced Asian tourist inflow.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Norwegian tourism growth expected to slow after strong years
viewpoints.description: Following several years of strong growth, contacts in Norway's household services sector, particularly tourism, anticipate a slowdown in growth. Despite the krone appreciation in recent months, the exchange rate is still reported to have a positive effect on demand; however, stronger competition from Airbnb and geopolitical events leading to cancellations from Asian customers are contributing to a more cautious outlook for the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 1/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish hotel investment market positive yet selective in 2026
viewpoints.description: The Irish hotel investment market is maintaining positive momentum in 2026, though deal activity is more selective following a landmark year in 2025 where transaction volumes exceeded €1.7 billion. Advisors note increased investor appetite for value-add opportunities, repositioning projects, and high-quality regional assets, shifting focus away from large portfolio trades. This indicates sustained confidence in underlying tourism fundamentals.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Encouraging demand faces margin constraints and increasing competition
viewpoints.description: Irish hospitality demand fundamentals are strong, driven by resilient overseas travel, robust domestic demand, and improved air access. However, inflationary pressures, labor availability challenges, and energy volatility continue to hinder margin recovery. Additionally, new, albeit limited, hotel supply in Dublin and Belfast is expected to intensify competitive pressure, requiring operators to focus on cost control and strategic positioning to ensure sustainable profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

new_opportunities.description: Travelers show a strong preference (63%) for curated lists of approximately ten recommended options over extensive catalogs or single AI-generated plans, indicating an opportunity for platforms and operators to provide credible, pre-selected shortlists based on preferences, budget, and trip type, with clear reasoning for each choice.

market_sizing.methodology: Survey of travelers on platform preferences for travel planning. 63% preferred a curated list of ten options, 30% preferred a full searchable catalog of 500 options, and 7% wanted a single AI-generated plan, given identical prices and inventory.
market_sizing.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted full year performance for Dublin hotels. Occupancy: 83.8%, Average Daily Rate (ADR): €176.11, Revenue Per Available Room (RevPAR): €147.53. Expected RevPAR growth of 1.1% over 2025.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

pnl_drivers.description: The pace of employment growth in the sector has slowed due to rising cost pressures, leading to critical reviews of staffing requirements, indicating a constraint on margin recovery.

market_sizing.methodology: Total employment in the Irish hospitality sector for the previous year (2025), representing 9% of total employees in the country.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

pnl_drivers.description: Increased wage costs are directly impacting the profitability of hospitality businesses, rising from 38.5% of turnover in 2023 to 39.5% in 2024, exacerbating margin pressures.

market_sizing.methodology: Average cost of wages as a percentage of turnover in the Irish hospitality sector, as reported by Crowe for year-end December 2024. This figure is up from 38.5% in 2023.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

market_sizing.methodology: Irish hotel investment market transaction volumes in 2025. Total volumes exceeded €1.7 billion, which was the strongest level ever recorded. Excluding the Dalata transaction, the volume was €600 million.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

new_opportunities.description: Investor appetite is increasing for assets that offer opportunities for operational improvement, repositioning, and value creation, particularly for high-quality regional properties.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted deal flow for the Irish hotel investment market in 2026, with advisors expecting steady active on and off-market deals combining to a value of around €350 million.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026
